he: שִׁיר מִזְמוֹר לְאָסָף׃
אֱלֹהִים אַל־דֳּמִי־לָךְ אַל־תֶּחֱרַשׁ וְאַל־תִּשְׁקֹט אֵל׃
כִּי־הִנֵּה אוֹיְבֶיךָ יֶהֱמָיוּן וּמְשַׂנְאֶיךָ נָשְׂאוּ רֹאשׁ׃
עַל־עַמְּךָ יַעֲרִימוּ סוֹד וְיִתְיָעֲצוּ עַל־צְפוּנֶיךָ׃
אָמְרוּ לְכוּ וְנַכְחִידֵם מִגּוֹי וְלֹא־יִזָּכֵר שֵׁם־יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹד׃
כִּי נוֹעֲצוּ לֵב יַחְדָּו עָלֶיךָ בְּרִית יִכְרֹתוּ׃
אָהֳלֵי אֱדוֹם וְיִשְׁמְעֵאלִים מוֹאָב וְהַגְרִים׃
גְּבָל וְעַמּוֹן וַעֲמָלֵק פְּלֶשֶׁת עִם־יֹשְׁבֵי צוֹר׃
גַּם־אַשּׁוּר נִלְוָה עִמָּם הָיוּ זְרוֹעַ לִבְנֵי־לוֹט סֶלָה׃
עֲשֵׂה־לָהֶם כְּמִדְיָן כְּסִיסְרָא כְיָבִין בְּנַחַל קִישׁוֹן׃
נִשְׁמְדוּ בְעֵין־דֹּאר הָיוּ דֹּמֶן לָאֲדָמָה׃
שִׁיתֵמוֹ נְדִיבֵמוֹ כְּעֹרֵב וְכִזְאֵב וּכְזֶבַח וּכְצַלְמֻנָּע כָּל־נְסִיכֵמוֹ׃
אֲשֶׁר אָמְרוּ נִירֲשָׁה לָּנוּ אֵת נְאוֹת אֱלֹהִים׃
אֱ‍לֹהַי שִׁיתֵמוֹ כַגַּלְגַּל כְּקַשׁ לִפְנֵי־רוּחַ׃
כְּאֵשׁ תִּבְעַר־יָעַר וּכְלֶהָבָה תְּלַהֵט הָרִים׃
כֵּן תִּרְדְּפֵם בְּסַעֲרֶךָ וּבְסוּפָתְךָ תְבַהֲלֵם׃
מַלֵּא פְנֵיהֶם קָלוֹן וִיבַקְשׁוּ שִׁמְךָ יְהוָה׃
יֵבֹשׁוּ וְיִבָּהֲלוּ עֲדֵי־עַד וְיַחְפְּרוּ וְיֹאבֵדוּ׃
וְיֵדְעוּ כִּי־אַתָּה שִׁמְךָ יְהוָה לְבַדֶּךָ עֶלְיוֹן עַל־כָּל־הָאָרֶץ׃
silverstein: A song, a psalm of Asaf.
O G d, do not remain silent [(to our abuses, wherein our enemies abuse us)]. Let the Almighty not be mute nor still.
For Your foes are tumultuous; Your haters have raised their heads.
They have been subtle in counsel against Your people. They have plotted against Your hidden ones [(Israel)].
They have said: Let us go and cut them off from [being] a nation; let the name of Israel be mentioned no more.
For they have taken heart-counsel together; they have entered into a covenant against You. [(You being known as "the G d of Israel," if they go lost, Your great name will not be mentioned.)]
The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moav and the Hagrites.
Geval, Ammon, and Amalek, Plasheth and the inhabitants of Tzor.
Ashur, too, [(who in the past avoided rash counsels)] joined them. They were [ever] a [mighty] arm to the sons of Lot [i.e., they abetted our neighbors, Ammon and Moav, in attacking us].
Do to them as [You did] to Midian [(through Gideon)]; to Sisra and to Yavin in the river-bed of Kishon [(through Barak)].
They were destroyed in Ein Dor; they were as dung on the ground.
Make their princes as ravens and wolves; and as Zevach and Tzalmuna [(princes of Midian slain by Gideon)] all of their lords.
Because they said: Let us inherit for ourselves the habitation of G d [i.e., the Temple].
O G d, make them as thistles, as stubble before the wind.
As a fire burning the forest, as a flame lighting up the mountains.
Thus pursue them with Your tempest, confound them with Your whirlwind.
Fill their faces with shame, till they seek Your name, O L rd.
They will be shamed and confounded forever; they will be abashed and go lost.
And [then all] will know that Your name alone is "L rd," that You are supreme over all the earth.
koren: A Poem, A Psalm of Asaf.
Do not keep silence, O God: do not hold Thy peace, and be still, O God.
For lo, Thy enemies make a tumult: and they who hate Thee have lifted up the head.
They take crafty counsel against Thy people, and consult against Thy hidden ones.
They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Yisra᾽el may be no more in remembrance.
For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against Thee:
the tents of Edom, and the Yishme᾽elim; of Mo᾽av, and the Hagrim;
Geval, and ῾Ammon, and ῾Amaleq; Peleshet with the inhabitants of Żor;
Ashshur also is joined with them: they are the strong arm of the children of Lot. (Sela.)
Do to them as to Midyan; as to Sisera, as to Yavin, at the wadi of Qishon:
who perished at ῾En-dor: they became like dung on the earth.
Make their nobles like ῾Orev, and like Ze᾽ev: and all their princes like Zevaĥ, and Żalmunna:
who said, Let us seize for our possession the pastures of God.
O my God, make them like the whirling chaff: like the stubble before the wind.
As the fire burns a wood, and as the flame sets the mountains on fire;
so pursue them with thy tempest, and terrify them with thy storm.
Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek thy name, O Lord.
Let them be confounded and affrighted forever; and let them be put to shame, and perish:
that men may know that thou alone, whose name is the Lord, art the most high over all the earth.

he: לַמְנַצֵּחַ עַל־הַגִּתִּית לִבְנֵי־קֹרַח מִזְמוֹר׃
מַה־יְּדִידוֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶיךָ יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת׃
נִכְסְפָה וְגַם־כָּלְתָה נַפְשִׁי לְחַצְרוֹת יְהוָה לִבִּי וּבְשָׂרִי יְרַנְּנוּ אֶל אֵל־חָי׃
גַּם־צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁתָה אֶפְרֹחֶיהָ אֶת־מִזְבְּחוֹתֶיךָ יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת מַלְכִּי וֵאלֹהָי׃
אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ עוֹד יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה׃
אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם עוֹז־לוֹ בָךְ מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם׃
עֹבְרֵי בְּעֵמֶק הַבָּכָא מַעְיָן יְשִׁיתוּהוּ גַּם־בְּרָכוֹת יַעְטֶה מוֹרֶה׃
יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל־חָיִל יֵרָאֶה אֶל־אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן׃
יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים צְבָאוֹת שִׁמְעָה תְפִלָּתִי הַאֲזִינָה אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה׃
מָגִנֵּנוּ רְאֵה אֱלֹהִים וְהַבֵּט פְּנֵי מְשִׁיחֶךָ׃
כִּי טוֹב־יוֹם בַּחֲצֵרֶיךָ מֵאָלֶף בָּחַרְתִּי הִסְתּוֹפֵף בְּבֵית אֱלֹהַי מִדּוּר בְּאָהֳלֵי־רֶשַׁע׃
כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים חֵן וְכָבוֹד יִתֵּן יְהוָה לֹא יִמְנַע־טוֹב לַהֹלְכִים בְּתָמִים׃
יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם בֹּטֵחַ בָּךְ׃
silverstein: For the conductor, on the gitith, of the sons of Korach, a psalm.
How beloved are Your dwellings, O L rd of hosts!
My soul desires and longs for the [(destroyed)] courts of the L rd. My heart and flesh sing [i.e., pray for their restoration] to the living G d.
Even a bird found a home [there in the ruins], and a swallow, a nest for itself, placing her fledglings upon Your altars, O L rd of hosts, my King and my G d.
Happy those who [will yet] dwell in Your house [and] who will praise You again, forever.
Happy the man whose strength is in You, who [contemplates the straightening of his] ways in his heart.

The transgressors in the vale of tears [(Gehinnom)] will make it a pool [with their weeping], while covering the "Teacher" with blessings [(saying: "Righteously did He judge us and righteous is His judgment!")]
They [("who dwell in Your house, etc.")] will go from strength to strength [(from the study hall to the house of prayer) and] they will appear before G d in Zion.
O L rd, G d of hosts, hearken to my prayer [(to rebuild Your Temple)]; listen, G d of Jacob, forever.
Our shield [i.e., the Temple], see [and remember], O G d, and regard the countenance of Your anointed one [(David, i.e., give heart to his efforts towards the building of the Temple)].

For better a day in Your courts [(and death the next day)] than [living] a thousand [years elsewhere]. I have chosen to sit on the threshold of the house of my G d rather than dwell [in luxury] in the tents of the wicked.
For sun and shield is the L rd G d. The L rd will grant grace and glory. He will not withhold good from those who walk in innocence.
O L rd of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You!
koren: To the chief Musician upon the Gittit, A Psalm for the sons of Qoraĥ.
How lovely are Thy dwelling places, O Lord of hosts!
My soul longs, indeed, it faints for the courts of the Lord: my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young. Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, my King, and my God –
happy are they who dwell in Thy house: they are ever praising thee. (Sela.)
Happy is the man whose strength is in Thee; in whose heart are Thy highways,
who, passing through the valley of Bakha, turn in into a waterspring; moreover, the early rain covers it with blessings.
They go from strength to strength, every one of them appears before God in Żiyyon.
O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: give ear, O God of Ya῾aqov. (Sela.)
Behold, O God, our shield, and look upon the face of Thy anointed.
For a day in Thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be at the threshold in the house of my God, than dwell in the tents of wickedness.
For the Lord God is a sun and shield: the Lord will give grace and honour: no good thing will he withhold from those who walk uprightly.
O Lord of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in Thee.

he: לַמְנַצֵּחַ לִבְנֵי־קֹרַח מִזְמוֹר׃
רָצִיתָ יְהוָה אַרְצֶךָ שַׁבְתָּ שבות [שְׁבִית] יַעֲקֹב׃
נָשָׂאתָ עֲוֺן עַמֶּךָ כִּסִּיתָ כָל־חַטָּאתָם סֶלָה׃
אָסַפְתָּ כָל־עֶבְרָתֶךָ הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ׃
שׁוּבֵנוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׁעֵנוּ וְהָפֵר כַּעַסְךָ עִמָּנוּ׃
הַלְעוֹלָם תֶּאֱנַף־בָּנוּ תִּמְשֹׁךְ אַפְּךָ לְדֹר וָדֹר׃
הֲלֹא־אַתָּה תָּשׁוּב תְּחַיֵּנוּ וְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂמְחוּ־בָךְ׃
הַרְאֵנוּ יְהוָה חַסְדֶּךָ וְיֶשְׁעֲךָ תִּתֶּן־לָנוּ׃
אֶשְׁמְעָה מַה־יְדַבֵּר הָאֵל יְהוָה כִּי יְדַבֵּר שָׁלוֹם אֶל־עַמּוֹ וְאֶל־חֲסִידָיו וְאַל־יָשׁוּבוּ לְכִסְלָה׃
אַךְ קָרוֹב לִירֵאָיו יִשְׁעוֹ לִשְׁכֹּן כָּבוֹד בְּאַרְצֵנוּ׃
חֶסֶד־וֶאֱמֶת נִפְגָּשׁוּ צֶדֶק וְשָׁלוֹם נָשָׁקוּ׃
אֱמֶת מֵאֶרֶץ תִּצְמָח וְצֶדֶק מִשָּׁמַיִם נִשְׁקָף׃
גַּם־יְהוָה יִתֵּן הַטּוֹב וְאַרְצֵנוּ תִּתֵּן יְבוּלָהּ׃
צֶדֶק לְפָנָיו יְהַלֵּךְ וְיָשֵׂם לְדֶרֶךְ פְּעָמָיו׃
silverstein: For the conductor, of the sons of Korach, a psalm.
You would conciliate, O L rd, Your land [(and Your world would be conciliated) if] You returned the captivity of Jacob
[and] You forgave the transgression of Your people [and] You concealed all of their sins forever
[and] You gathered in all of Your wrath [and] You turned from Your burning wrath.
[So turn and] return us, O G d of our salvation, and annul Your anger against us.
Will You be angry with us forever? Will Your wrath stretch out throughout the generations?
Will You not [in the end] return and give us life [(as You have assured us through Your prophets)], and will Your people not rejoice in You?
[Therefore,] show us [swiftly], O L rd, Your lovingkindness, and confer Your salvation upon us.
Let me [merit to] hear what the Almighty L rd speaks when He speaks peace to His people and to His saints, and let them not return to their folly.
Very close to those who fear Him is His salvation, to reposit glory in our land.

Lovingkindness and truth have met [i.e., When Israel speak truth, lovingkindness will greet them from heaven.] Righteousness and peace have kissed [i.e., the reward of righteousness will be peace (viz. Isaiah 32:17)].
[When] truth sprouts from the earth [(i.e., When Israel speaks truth], righteousness [(the righteousness that they perform on earth)] will be reflected from heaven.
The L rd, too, will give good [(He will open His heavenly treasure trove to give rain)] and our land will give forth its produce.
Righteousness will go before Him, and He will place [righteousness] in the way of His steps [(wherein He leads His children)].
koren: To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Qoraĥ.
Lord, Thou hast been favourable to Thy land: Thou hast brought back the captivity of Ya῾aqov.
Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of Thy people, Thou hast pardoned all their sin. (Sela.)
Thou hast withdrawn all Thy wrath: Thou hast turned from the fierceness of Thy anger.
Restore us, O God of our salvation, and cause Thy anger towards us to cease.
Wilt Thou be angry with us forever? Wilt Thou draw out Thy anger to all generations?
Wilt Thou not revive us again: that Thy people may rejoice in Thee?
Show us thy mercy, O Lord, and grant us Thy salvation.
I will hear what God the Lord will speak: for he will speak peace to his people, and to his pious ones: but let them not turn back to folly.
Surely his salvation is near to them who fear him; that glory may dwell in our land.
Love and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
Truth will spring out of the earth; and righteousness will look down from heaven.
The Lord moreover shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield its increase.
Righteousness shall go before him, and walk in the way of his steps.

he: תְּפִלָּה לְדָוִד הַטֵּה־יְהוָה אָזְנְךָ עֲנֵנִי כִּי־עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן אָנִי׃
שָׁמְרָה נַפְשִׁי כִּי־חָסִיד אָנִי הוֹשַׁע עַבְדְּךָ אַתָּה אֱלֹהַי הַבּוֹטֵחַ אֵלֶיךָ׃
חָנֵּנִי אֲדֹנָי כִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֶקְרָא כָּל־הַיּוֹם׃
שַׂמֵּחַ נֶפֶשׁ עַבְדֶּךָ כִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֲדֹנָי נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא׃
כִּי־אַתָּה אֲדֹנָי טוֹב וְסַלָּח וְרַב־חֶסֶד לְכָל־קֹרְאֶיךָ׃
הַאֲזִינָה יְהוָה תְּפִלָּתִי וְהַקְשִׁיבָה בְּקוֹל תַּחֲנוּנוֹתָי׃
בְּיוֹם צָרָתִי אֶקְרָאֶךָּ כִּי תַעֲנֵנִי׃
אֵין־כָּמוֹךָ בָאֱלֹהִים אֲדֹנָי וְאֵין כְּמַעֲשֶׂיךָ׃
כָּל־גּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ יָבוֹאוּ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְפָנֶיךָ אֲדֹנָי וִיכַבְּדוּ לִשְׁמֶךָ׃
כִּי־גָדוֹל אַתָּה וְעֹשֵׂה נִפְלָאוֹת אַתָּה אֱלֹהִים לְבַדֶּךָ׃
הוֹרֵנִי יְהוָה דַּרְכֶּךָ אֲהַלֵּךְ בַּאֲמִתֶּךָ יַחֵד לְבָבִי לְיִרְאָה שְׁמֶךָ׃
אוֹדְךָ אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהַי בְּכָל־לְבָבִי וַאֲכַבְּדָה שִׁמְךָ לְעוֹלָם׃
כִּי־חַסְדְּךָ גָּדוֹל עָלָי וְהִצַּלְתָּ נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּיָּה׃
אֱלֹהִים זֵדִים קָמוּ־עָלַי וַעֲדַת עָרִיצִים בִּקְשׁוּ נַפְשִׁי וְלֹא שָׂמוּךָ לְנֶגְדָּם׃
וְאַתָּה אֲדֹנָי אֵל־רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת׃
פְּנֵה אֵלַי וְחָנֵּנִי תְּנָה־עֻזְּךָ לְעַבְדֶּךָ וְהוֹשִׁיעָה לְבֶן־אֲמָתֶךָ׃
עֲשֵׂה־עִמִּי אוֹת לְטוֹבָה וְיִרְאוּ שֹׂנְאַי וְיֵבֹשׁוּ כִּי־אַתָּה יְהוָה עֲזַרְתַּנִי וְנִחַמְתָּנִי׃
silverstein: A prayer of David. Incline, O L rd, Your ear, and answer me; for I am poor and destitute.
Guard my soul for I am saintly [(remaining silent to insult and abuse though I have the power to avenge myself)]. Help Your servant (You, my G d), who trusts in You.
Be gracious unto me, O L rd, for unto You do I call all the day.
Rejoice the soul of Your servant, for unto You, O L rd, do I lift my soul [i.e., direct my heart].
For You, O L rd, are good and forgiving, and profuse in lovingkindness to all who call upon You.
Hear, O L rd, my prayer, and give ear to the voice of my supplications.
I call You in the day of my distress, [confident] that You will answer me.
There is none like You among the heavenly ones, O L rd, and there are none like Your deeds.
All the nations that You made will come and bow down before You, O L rd, and they will give honor to Your name.

For You are great and perform wonders, You, G d, alone. [(Heaven and earth were created before the angels were created, wherefore the nations will honor Your name alone (as the Creator, and not theirs)].
Teach me, O L rd, Your ways, so that I may walk in Your truth. Make my heart one, in fear of Your name.
I shall thank You, O L rd my G d, with all of my heart, and I shall extol Your name forever.
For Your lovingkindness is great upon me, and You have rescued my soul from the nether sheol [(whither adulterers are relegated) by removing my transgression [with Bathsheva, viz. II Samuel 12:13].
O G d, evil-doers have arisen against me, and the assembly of the arrogant have sought my soul and not placed You [i.e., Your fear] before their faces.
And You, O L rd, are a merciful and gracious G d, withholding wrath and profuse in lovingkindness and in truth.
Turn to me and be gracious unto me; give Your strength to Your servant and save the son of Your maidservant [(who humbles himself even more than a bought servant)].
Set up for me a sign of good, and let my foes see it and be abashed; for You, O L rd, have [ever] helped me and consoled me.
koren: A Prayer of David. Incline Thy ear, O Lord, hear me: for I am poor and needy.
Preserve my soul; for I am godly: O Thou my God, save Thy servant who trusts in Thee.
Be gracious to me, O Lord: for I cry to Thee daily.
Rejoice the soul of Thy servant: for to Thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.
For Thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive; and of bountiful love towards all those who call upon Thee.
Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplications.
On the day of my trouble I will call upon Thee: for Thou wilt answer me.
Among the gods there is none like Thee, O Lord; nor are there any works like Thine.
All nations whom Thou hast made shall come and prostrate themselves before Thee, O Lord; and shall glorify Thy name.
For Thou art great, and doest wondrous things: Thou art God alone.
Teach me Thy way, O Lord; I will walk in Thy truth: make my heart single to fear Thy name.
I will thank Thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart: and I will glorify Thy name for evermore.
For great is Thy steadfast love towards me: and Thou hast delivered my soul from the depths of She᾽ol.
O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assembly of violent men have sought after my soul; and have not set Thee before them.
But Thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and bountiful in love and truth.
O turn to me, and have mercy upon me; give Thy strength to Thy servant, and save the son of Thy handmaid.
Show me a sign for good; that they who hate me may see it, and be ashamed: because Thou, Lord, hast helped me, and comforted me.

he: לִבְנֵי־קֹרַח מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר יְסוּדָתוֹ בְּהַרְרֵי־קֹדֶשׁ׃
אֹהֵב יְהוָה שַׁעֲרֵי צִיּוֹן מִכֹּל מִשְׁכְּנוֹת יַעֲקֹב׃
נִכְבָּדוֹת מְדֻבָּר בָּךְ עִיר הָאֱלֹהִים סֶלָה׃
אַזְכִּיר רַהַב וּבָבֶל לְיֹדְעָי הִנֵּה פְלֶשֶׁת וְצוֹר עִם־כּוּשׁ זֶה יֻלַּד־שָׁם׃
וּלֲצִיּוֹן יֵאָמַר אִישׁ וְאִישׁ יֻלַּד־בָּהּ וְהוּא יְכוֹנְנֶהָ עֶלְיוֹן׃
יְהוָה יִסְפֹּר בִּכְתוֹב עַמִּים זֶה יֻלַּד־שָׁם סֶלָה׃
וְשָׁרִים כְּחֹלְלִים כָּל־מַעְיָנַי בָּךְ׃
silverstein: Of the sons of Korach, a psalm, a song founded on the holy mountains [Zion and Jerusalem].
The L rd loves the gates of Zion more than all the habitations of Jacob.
Glories were spoken of you [by G d, Jerusalem] — [that] you are the city of G d forever.

[(And He spoke this, too:)] I shall put Egypt and Bavel in mind of My beloved [(to bring them as a gift to the L rd in Jerusalem. viz. Isaiah 66:20)]; likewise, Plesheth, Tzor and Kush, [(saying, as they bring them:)] "This one was born there." [viz. Isaiah 27:12].
And to Zion it will be said of each one that he was born in her [and is being returned]. And He shall establish it as supreme [over all the cities].

In time to come, [when] the L rd inscribes the [idolatrous] peoples [for destruction], He will count [the Jews swallowed up amongst them, and, taking them from their midst, will say:] "This one was born there." [viz. Isaiah 66:21]
And revelers will sing [thereupon]: "All of my innards are with You!" [i.e., with Your salvation.]
koren: A Psalm for the sons of Qoraĥ, A Poem. His foundation is in the holy mountains.
The Lord loves the gates of Żiyyon more than all the dwellings of Ya῾aqov.
Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. (Sela.)
I will make mention of Rahav and Bavel to those who know me: behold Peleshet, and Żor, with Kush, saying, Such a man was born there.
But of Żiyyon it shall be said, This and that man was born in her: and the highest himself shall establish her.
The Lord shall record, when he registers the peoples, that this man was born there. (Sela.)
And singers and dancers alike, shall say, All my springs are in Thee.
